html:
A military barracks in Conakry used as a political prison under Sekou Toure, where thousands of people were held, tortured and killed between the 1960s and 1984.

After each alleged plot, ministers, officers, traders and teachers were arrested, forced to confess on radio and often starved to death in the black diet. Among those who died there were Diallo Telli, the first secretary-general of the Organisation of African Unity, and Fodeba Keita, founder of Les Ballets Africains. The Fula people suffered especially after 1976. The camp was closed after the 1984 coup by Lansana Conte, and families still seek the remains of the dead.
sum: A military barracks in Conakry used as a political prison under Sekou Toure, where thousands of people were held, tortured and killed between the 1960s and 1984.
